question: A standard die is rolled six times. What is the probability that the product of all six rolls is odd? Express your answer as a common fraction.
solution:
A product is odd exactly when every factor is odd, so all six rolls must be odd. On each roll, three of the six outcomes (1, 3, 5) are odd, giving probability 3/6 = 1/2. Since the rolls are independent, the probability that all six are odd is (1/2)^6 = 1/64.
Final answer: \frac{1}{64}
